Details

Every figure included by main.tex, in paper order. Status from the change log papers/paper1/figure_log.toml (not ready → in work → for review → accepted); the 11-02 review verdicts stay on each slide as the second chip. Rebuild: papers/paper1/make_figures_deck.py.

What “publication-ready” means here: the checklist every figure has to pass

JINST, full text width ≈ 15.5 cm; applied one figure at a time with Dylan

standard
Sizedrawn at the width it is printed (full width 6.1 in, half 3.0 in); no rescaling in LaTeX; type 7–9 pt in print
No titles insidethe caption carries the title; panels labelled (a), (b), … in a corner
Axesevery axis labelled with quantity and unit in mathtext; sensible ticks; ranges that show the data, shared where compared
Chamberspaper palette only (det3 dark blue on top); X solid, Y dashed open; det4 grey
Data vs modeldata as markers with error bars; models/fits as lines; the claim visible without reading the caption
Legendonly what the reader needs; off the data; one per figure if panels share it
Inkno gridline clutter, no boxes, no superfluous annotations; text in the plot only for the one point it makes
Numbersevery plotted number traceable: the figure ships its CSV; caption and text quote the same values
VectorPDF, embedded fonts; rasters only for maps/displays, at ≥ 300 dpi

for review keep  Introduction

2026-11-03: New (replaces microtpc_principle): full-width row, a minimal sketch on the same vertical scale as the data (t = t0 + z/v), data and model of event 788…

8

Details

Caption (draft): TPC operation. (a) The chamber in section (the stage below the mesh enlarged): the ionisation left along the track drifts straight down to the mesh and arrives later the higher it started, t=t_0+z/v; the avalanche lands on the resistive strips, which couple it to the readout strips below. (b) The X view of a real chamber A cosmic muon (Run 1), amplitude per strip and 60 ns sample, on the same vertical scale as (a): the track appears as a slanted column from the mesh (t_0) to the cathode (t_0+g/v, grey lines). Dashed black: the reference track; dashed vermillion: the fitted track. (c) The forward model at the fit, same colour scale: the whole strip × time picture is fitted, not per-strip times. Each pulse lasts a few samples after its electrons arrive (the shaping), so the charge extends above the cathode line.

9

Details

Caption (draft): What one chamber sees: four chamber A events of Run 1, both views (strip position against drift time, one colour scale in ADC; grey lines: mesh and cathode). (a) A cosmic muon with the reference track (dashed black) and the fit (dashed vermillion). (b) A muon with a δ-ray knocked sideways at mid-gap. (c) A muon (right in X, left in Y) next to a low-energy electron curling through the gap. (d) Two particles, each fitted (vermillion, amber). A view whose particles lie far apart is drawn as a broken axis (//); all panels share one mm scale across the strips and, in (a) and (b), the same scale in depth (z=v (t-t_0)), so those are true images of the tracks in the strip–depth plane.

2026-11-03: Made from the production gerbers: pads, X/Y strips, fan-out, connectors, passivated y ends, pad-via checkerboard zoom. Orientation assumes local = ger…

Pads → X/Y strips, the 18 mm passivated y ends, the unpassivated x sides

Ties the design notes (§2.1) to the edge section

11

Details

Caption (draft): Readout board, top view (detector-local frame, from the production gerbers). (a) 512×512 pads of 0.68 mm on a 0.78 mm pitch cover 399.4×399.4 mm^2. The Y strips (L5, green) run along y to two connectors on the +y edge and the X strips (L6, orange) along x to two connectors on the +x edge. The resistive strips (dashed outline: the deposit) run along y and are passivated over 18.0 mm (low y) and 18.7 mm (high y) at their ends (hatched), leaving a measured efficient area of 399.4×359.9 mm^2; the x sides are not passivated. (b) A pad window: each pad is connected by a via to a Y strip or an X strip in a checkerboard pattern, so every strip collects every second pad along its length. (c) The fan-out of the Y strips to one of the connector blocks (300 contact pads each). Only the strips with copper on their own layer are drawn; the others leave the layer by a via to L7.

Fix: A photo or Gerber render from Stephan plus an overlay of the measured efficient area 399.4 × 359.9 mm².

2026-11-03: New: strip-sum signal vs drift time, A on the bench flat, E at SPS falling (CF4 and CO2), with gas-fit models with/without O2.

30

Details

Caption (draft): Charge against drift time. A head-on track deposits charge uniformly across the gap, so the strip-sum signal against time is the charge collected from each depth. (a) Chamber A on the bench (248 V/cm) stays flat to the end of the column; chamber E at SPS falls with drift time in both gas families (Ar/CF_4/iC_4H_10, run 71, 251 V/cm; Ar/CO_2, run 55, 251 V/cm): electrons from the far side of the gap are lost to attachment. Each curve is normalised to its plateau 250–450 ns after the column start. (b, c) The same E stacks with the gas-fit model including O_2 (226 and 443 ppm, solid) and with the same water but no O_2 (dashed), which stays flat and fails (χ^2 842 and 10 600 against 49 and 258 for 55 points). The columns last longer at SPS because the drift velocity is lower in these mixtures; run 55 was zero-suppressed, and the fit includes the distortion this causes.

Appendix: event-display styles to choose from

Same four chamber A events in each style (made by papers/paper1/figs/make_displays.py gallery)

A: white to navy (the paper default for now)   The 11-02 colours, now in ADC on one scale for both views.

B: magma (white, yellow, red, black)   High contrast; faint charge reads well; fits drawn blue.

C: grey data, coloured lines   The lines pop most; the data recede; prints well in black and white.

D: viridis   Perceptually uniform; yellow for low charge can look washed out on white.

E: dark background, inferno   The most striking on screen; heavy in print and for a journal page.

Reference track: dashed with a halo (default)   Thicker than the fits; black in A.

Reference track: translucent band + thin line   Marks the reference without covering the data.

Reference track: thin line + arrowheads outside the gap   Points at where the reference enters and leaves.

Colour scale sqrt(ADC)   Faint charge brighter; the MIP core saturates the scale.

Views separated by a small gap   For comparison with the abutting default.

Zoomed to the charge (depth not to the strip scale)   The default draws depth and strips on one mm scale where the window allows.
